title: AT THE BLAST OF YOUR NOSTRILS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"In the greatness of your majesty you threw down those who opposed you. You
unleashed your burning anger; it consumed them like stubble. By the blast of
your nostrils the waters piled up. The surging waters stood up like a wall; the
deep waters congealed in the heart of the sea." - Ex 15:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is vivid, physical poetry. God breathes, and the sea stands up.

We should read it as the poetry it is. God does not have nostrils. The song is
using human imagery to say something true: what took the whole night and a
strong east wind was, from God's side, no more effort than a breath.

That is worth sitting with. What overwhelms us entirely costs God nothing. The
sea that Israel could not have crossed in a thousand years moved at a breath.

Notice the word "congealed." The waters became solid, held, stacked. The most
formless, uncontrollable thing in the ancient imagination, the deep, stood still
and behaved.

Jesus stepped into a boat one night and the disciples woke Him in terror as the
storm broke over them. He stood up, spoke to the wind and the waves, and it was
completely calm. Their question afterwards is the right one: "Who is this? Even
the wind and the waves obey him!" (Mark 4:41).

The answer is in this song. The One whose breath piles up the sea had been asleep
in their boat.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What feels uncontrollable to you right now?
2. Does it help to know that what overwhelms you costs God nothing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, what is impossible to me is a breath to You. Help me to bring my
impossible things to You instead of carrying them alone. Amen.
